root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Define f(x) = floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (floor of k times x) divided by k. Determine the set of real numbers x for which f(x) is a global maximum among all real y, and determine the value of that global maximum.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every real r with 0 <= r < 1, if m is defined as the floor of n times r, then f_n(r) is at most f_n(m divided by n).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with 0 <= r < 1
let m be floor of n times r
claim: f_n(r) <= f_n(m divided by n)

payload.statement_nl: Let n > 1 and let f_n be defined as above. For any real r with 0 <= r < 1, if m = floor(n*r), then f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: No previous feedback was provided; the proof was revised directly from the statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: Since m=⌊nr⌋ implies m/n<=r, each floor term satisfies ⌊k(m/n)⌋<=⌊kr⌋ for 1<=k<=n, while the leading term ⌊nr⌋ equals ⌊n(m/n)⌋. Substituting gives f_n(r)<=f_n(m/n).
